answer: A refundable stake bond resists Sybil attacks by making each identity expensive. To join, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if it is caught running duplicate identities or spamming votes. One honest agent pays once; an attacker who wants an ocean of fake accounts must fund every one, so the cost grows linearly with the attack. Reputation then accrues to the bonded identity like a jade seal, hard to forge and easy to verify, and a violet flag from peers triggers an audit before the bond is returned. The bond, not a password, is the price of admission.
